title: 4-bit Priority Encoder
statement:
Find the highest-priority set bit in a 4-bit value and report its index.

## Your entity

```
entity solution is
    port (
        data  : in  std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        index : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0);
        valid : out std_logic
    );
end entity solution;
```

`index` is the position of the *most significant* `'1'` in `data` -- bit 3
outranks bit 2, which outranks bit 1, which outranks bit 0. `valid` is
`'1'` whenever at least one bit is set; when `data` is all zero, `valid`
must be `'0'` and `index` must be `"00"`.

`"0110"` has bits 1 and 2 set; bit 2 has the higher priority, so
`index = "10"`, `valid = '1'`. `"0000"` gives `index = "00"`,
`valid = '0'`.

## Input and output

The testbench reads one line of stdin as a 4-character bit string, drives
it onto `data`, waits for the output to settle, and writes `index`
immediately followed by `valid` back out on one line (three characters:
two for `index`, one for `valid`).

## Watch out

- A priority chain like this is usually written as an `if` /
  `elsif` / ... / `elsif` ladder, checked from the highest-priority bit
  down. The all-zero case is what falls through every one of those
  conditions -- it needs its own branch, with its own explicit values for
  *both* outputs. A ladder with no final `else` still elaborates and runs;
  it just leaves `index` and `valid` undefined for exactly the one input
  that never took any of the earlier branches, and undefined does not
  quietly become `'0'` -- ask for it and you get back `'U'`, GHDL's honest
  answer for "nothing ever drove this".

tests.name: none set
tests.description: The case every branch of an if/elsif ladder falls through -- it needs a branch of its own.

tests.name: two bits, higher wins
tests.description: Bits 1 and 2 are both set; index reports 2, not 1 -- the lower one is outranked, not ignored, so it still needs to make valid true, just not to set the index.

tests.name: every bit set
tests.description: Only the top bit's priority should show up in the answer.
